core_question.answer: Can frontier models produce economically valuable real-world professional deliverables that experts judge competitive with human work?

evidence.snippet: introducing GDPval: a new evaluation designed to help us track how well our models and others perform on economically valuable, real-world tasks
It measures model performance on tasks drawn directly from the real-world knowledge work of experienced professionals

motivation.answer: GDPval is motivated by the gap between exam-style or short-answer benchmarks and the quality requirements of real occupational work products. It aims to evaluate whether models can complete economically valuable tasks, not only answer isolated questions.

evidence.snippet: classic academic benchmarks like MMLU (exam-style questions across dozens of subjects)
providing a clearer picture on how models perform on economically valuable tasks

answer: long-form document, spreadsheet, presentation, diagram, plan, brief, and blueprint generation

evidence.snippet: tasks drawn directly from the real-world knowledge work of experienced professionals across a wide range of occupations and sectors
documents, slides, diagrams, spreadsheets, care plans, briefs, and blueprints

benchmark_design.data_source: Tasks are drawn from real-world knowledge work across 9 U.S. GDP-linked industries and 44 occupations.
benchmark_design.task_construction: Each task asks a model to produce a professional work artifact using a prompt and associated reference files, rather than producing a short answer.
benchmark_design.expert_involvement: Tasks are crafted and vetted by experienced professionals; task writers also create scoring rubrics.

evidence.snippet: GDPval covers tasks across 9 industries and 44 occupations
The GDPval full set includes 1,320 specialized tasks (220 in the gold open-sourced set)
each meticulously crafted and vetted by experienced professionals with over 14 years of experience on average

rubric_gold_scoring.gold_definition: The gold reference is human expert work products and expert preference or quality judgments over model outputs versus human deliverables.
rubric_gold_scoring.scoring_protocol: Experts perform blind comparison between model outputs and human deliverables. Task-specific scoring rubrics are used to add consistency and transparency. Automated grading is described as an experimental direction rather than the sole scoring basis.
rubric_gold_scoring.judge_type: human expert blind review, with automated grader as experimental support
rubric_gold_scoring.human_review: Yes. Expert human judgment is central to the evaluation.

evidence.snippet: Task writers also created detailed scoring rubrics for their occupations
add consistency and transparency to the grading process

model_results.score: not recorded in this draft gold note

evidence.snippet: Early GDPval results show that models can already take on some repetitive, well-specified tasks faster and at lower cost than experts.

main_conclusions.claim: Real-work benchmarks should evaluate usefulness and expert-perceived artifact quality, not only short-answer correctness.
GDPval is intended to ground discussions of AI progress in evidence about occupational work.

evidence.snippet: help ground conversations about future AI improvements in evidence rather than guesswork

main_conclusions.claim: The benchmark authors expect future versions to become more interactive and context-rich.

evidence.snippet: Future versions will extend to more interactive workflows and context-rich tasks

failure_modes.explanation: Model outputs may look plausible while missing details that professional reviewers care about. This is an annotator synthesis from the benchmark's focus on expert artifact quality and needs a second-source check before review status.

evidence.snippet: real-world knowledge work of experienced professionals

failure_modes.explanation: Because GDPval tasks include documents, slides, spreadsheets, diagrams, and other deliverables, models may fail on structure, formatting, and artifact-level constraints. This should be checked against the official limitations section before final use.

evidence.snippet: documents, slides, diagrams, spreadsheets, care plans, briefs, and blueprints

failure_modes.explanation: Automated grading may not fully capture expert quality judgments, especially for complex professional deliverables.

reliability_notes.note: The full set is larger than the public gold set, so reproducibility depends on the released subset and available grading materials.
